questions.q: What is the key difference between GROUP BY and a window function using OVER()?
options: GROUP BY collapses rows into one per group; a window function keeps every original row while still computing a group-based value
They are functionally identical in every case
OVER() can only be used with COUNT, never AVG or SUM
GROUP BY is faster in every scenario
questions.explain: This is the defining distinction — window functions compute using a group but never reduce the row count.

questions.q: What does OVER() do to a function like AVG()?
options: Turns it into a window function that computes across related rows without collapsing the result set
Converts it into a scalar subquery
Removes its ability to use PARTITION BY
Makes it run once per column instead of once per row
questions.explain: AVG(ListPrice) OVER (PARTITION BY Color) shows the average per color, attached to every individual row.

questions.q: What does PARTITION BY do inside OVER()?
options: Divides rows into groups for the window function's calculation only, without collapsing the result set
Deletes rows outside the specified partition
Sorts the entire result set by the partition column
It has no effect unless combined with GROUP BY
questions.explain: PARTITION BY groups rows the way GROUP BY does, but purely for the window function's math — every row still appears individually.

options: ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), DENSE_RANK(), and NTILE()

Only aggregate functions from Chapter 4
